points.text: States speed = distance / time and divides 100 by 20
Gives 5 m/s and states a direction must be given for a velocity

items.prompt: An athlete sprints 100 metres in 20 seconds. Calculate her speed, and state the one extra fact that turns that speed into a velocity.

points.text: States acceleration is the gradient of a velocity-time graph, 20 / 10
Gives an acceleration of 2 metres per second squared

items.prompt: A velocity-time graph rises from 0 to 20 m/s in 10 seconds. Calculate the acceleration, using the gradient of the graph.

points.text: States pressure = force / area and divides 200 by 0.5
Gives a pressure of 400 Pa with unit

items.prompt: A crate of weight 200 N rests on a face of area 0.5 square metres. Calculate the pressure on the ground.

points.text: States the driving wheel pushes backward on the road at the contact patch, so friction on the wheel acts forwards
States friction opposes the relative slide between the surfaces, not the motion of the car

items.prompt: Explain how friction at a driving wheel can push a car forwards, even though friction is said to oppose motion.

levels.descriptor: Explanations chain graph readings and force ideas to the answer in order, with each step justified by a named gradient, area or force rule.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Explanations are broadly sound but one link between the graph or the forces and the answer is asserted rather than justified.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Answers state numbers or force names without connecting them into an explanation.
levels.label: Beginning
